newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Barley Board forecasts steady pool price.
newsitem.headline: Australia Barley Board forecasts steady pool price.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board (ABB) continues to forecast gross pool returns for 1997/98 at A$190.00 a tonne for malting barley and A$150.00 a tonne for feed barley, it said in a statement.

Announcing the monthly revision of pool returns, ABB chief executive officer Michael Iwaniw said market discussion on the coming harvest was currently dominated by crop potential in the major producing countries.
A near-bull market began in the second half of April as major concerns developed about the condition of crops in Europe and seeding delays in Canada, Iwaniw said.
While dry weather in Europe would have set crops back, extensive rain eventually fell, with crops reported to have responded well, he said.
The degree of any production loss would not be known until the European harvest started in July, he said.
In Canada, the wintry weather that caused seeding delays for spring barley was eventually followed by ideal conditions.
Although the area sown was reduced, above average crops were now expected, he said.
Low malting barley production in Australia would have a positive effect on prices, he said.

But with ther Australian season just started, major factors affecting market outlook at present were crops in Europe and speculation about what subsidy levels might be set by the European Commission, he said.
Canada had a significant carryover last year and Europe's bumper season re-built stocks from the record lows of two years ago. European policy this year would be crucial, he said.
"It is early days for the barley market, so for the present our forecasts remain steady, with attention in the immediate future focused on (the) European crop," he said.

On Tuesday, Australia's official commodities forecast agency the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) forecast that Australia's 1997/98 barley production would fall by almost 40 percent to about 4.12 million tonnes.
It also forecast that Australian barley prices would fall, to A$148.00 a tonne from A$160.00 on a composite feed/malting price basis.
